    {
      "startEvent": 0,
      "endEvent": 14,
      "reason": "Opening edited montage replaying the later design, natural-law, and miracle exchange, including material at E755–757, E713–717, and E1383–1390."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 23,
      "endEvent": 27,
      "reason": "Promotional insertion of a speaker excerpt from the advertised bonus conversation, with presenter speech at its boundaries; excluded as editorial material."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2422,
      "endEvent": 2424,
      "reason": "Brief bonus-conversation preview embedded in the closing newsletter advertisement; not a renewed argument in this debate."
    }
  ],
  "candidates": [
    {
      "startEvent": 738,
      "endEvent": 742,
      "contextStartEvent": 693,
      "contextEndEvent": 742,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "i'm always a little careful when i say well god should have done this differently",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["identity"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The closing appeal to the human–divine distinction could discount criticism of God's choices without explaining those choices. However, Collins supplies specific considerations about time, mathematical order, and evolution at E697–735, and acknowledges the questions as appropriate at E693–695. The text does not clearly make every objection illegitimate."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 775,
      "endEvent": 814,
      "contextStartEvent": 743,
      "contextEndEvent": 838,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "it is a betrayal of everything that darwinism seems to me stands for",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["shame", "identity"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Repeated betrayal language moves from evolution's explanatory sufficiency to rejecting an originating designer, without clearly earning that stronger step. Yet E769–789 supplies the simplicity-to-complexity argument, and E830–838 allows cosmology might support God. This is a genuinely uncertain rhetorical substitution, not an established exclusion of criticism regardless of merits."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1390,
      "endEvent": 1397,
      "contextStartEvent": 1349,
      "contextEndEvent": 1421,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "except extreme exceptions where god has a message for people that he cares about",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["comfort"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Divine messages provide an exception to the natural-order explanation of nonintervention, potentially accommodating both intervention and its absence. But Collins limits exceptions to major revelations and gives a predictability rationale at E1410–1419. He does not explicitly make arbitrary outcomes confirming evidence; this remains an uncertain protective argument, not a slogan."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1767,
      "endEvent": 1774,
      "contextStartEvent": 1739,
      "contextEndEvent": 1851,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "those moments of remarkable importance to convey a message to his creatures",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "After Dawkins renews the inconsistency objection, Collins again invokes God's communicative purposes to permit exceptions. The missing criterion is why these interventions warrant suspending laws while disaster prevention does not. However, E1819–1823 specifies the incarnation, and E1843–1845 explicitly welcomes arguments against miracle reports, limiting any claim of blanket protection."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2066,
      "endEvent": 2073,
      "contextStartEvent": 2030,
      "contextEndEvent": 2100,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "good is what good people do and evil is what bad people do",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The circular formulation could substitute labels for an account of what makes conduct good or evil. In context, however, Dawkins is resisting the reification of evil into a separate spirit, subsequently illustrating that distinction with cruelty at E2095–2100. His earlier evolutionary account also supplies reasons about moral dispositions, though not moral authority."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2127,
      "endEvent": 2131,
      "contextStartEvent": 2101,
      "contextEndEvent": 2183,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "it would be a horrible world to live in if we did",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": ["fear"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The compact condemnation dismisses the Abrahamic religions as moral sources without supplying examples or explaining why their moral teachings entail a horrible world. E2134–2183 provides a substantive account of changing moral norms and social influences, but does not establish this separate condemnation. No mechanism shields the assertion from objections."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2389,
      "endEvent": 2393,
      "contextStartEvent": 2343,
      "contextEndEvent": 2397,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "beauty is not something we should dismiss as just evolutionary epiphenomenal froth on the surface of an uncaring universe",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": ["ridicule"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Collins endorses the quoted aphorism after Dawkins expressly distinguishes explanation from demeaning beauty at E2374–2387. The 'froth' image substitutes a degrading characterization for a reason that an evolutionary account diminishes value. Collins previously offers experiential considerations at E2354–2373, but these do not establish that implication. No explicit protection blocks criticism."
    }
  ],
  "contrasts": [
    {
      "startEvent": 2030,
      "endEvent": 2058,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "not dismiss it but redo it because i think it was still a bit uh uh a bit unformed",
      "explanation": "Collins acknowledges Dawkins's criticism, proposes revising his moral argument, distinguishes cultural judgments from the existence of moral categories, and grants a possible evolutionary account. This is qualified reasoning open to revision."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1930,
      "endEvent": 2001,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "but the rule of thumb is still there",
      "explanation": "The compact phrase summarizes an explicit proposed mechanism: dispositions selected amid kinship and repeated interaction can persist outside those conditions, analogously to sexual desire with contraception. It does explanatory work supported by the surrounding argument."
    }
  ]
